units.text: Major sins affect a person's Islam
Q: What is the ruling on committing some sins, especially major sins? Does that affect a person's adherence to Islam?

A: Yes, it affects that. Committing major sins such as adultery, drinking alcohol, killing a soul without right, consuming riba (usury), backbiting, tale-bearing, and other sins affects and weakens one's Tawhid (monotheism) and faith. However, a Muslim does not become a disbeliever by any of that unless he regards it as permissible. This is contrary to the Khawarij, who declare a Muslim to be a disbeliever for committing a sin such as adultery, theft, or disobedience to parents, and other major sins, even if he does not regard them as permissible. This is a grave error on the part of the Khawarij. Ahlus-Sunnah wal-Jama'ah do not declare him a disbeliever for that, nor do they say he will abide in the Fire forever. Rather, they say he has deficient faith and Tawhid, but he is not guilty of major kufr (disbelief); rather his faith has deficiency and weakness.
For this reason, Allah has prescribed for the adulterer the hadd (prescribed punishment) of flogging: if he is a bikr (someone who has not previously consummated a valid marriage), he is flogged one hundred lashes and exiled for a year. Likewise, the drinker of intoxicants is flogged and not killed. Likewise, the thief's hand is cut off and he is not killed. If adultery, drinking intoxicants, and theft necessitated major kufr, they would be killed, because the Prophet ﷺ said: 'Whoever changes his religion, kill him.' Narrated by Imam al-Bukhari, may Allah have mercy on him, in his Sahih. This indicates that these sins are not apostasy; rather they weaken and diminish faith. Therefore, Allah has prescribed disciplining them with these hudud (punishments) so that they may repent and return to their Lord and be deterred from what their Lord, Glorified be He, has forbidden them.
The Mu'tazilah said that the sinner is in a station between two stations, but he will abide in the Fire forever if he dies upon that. Thus, they opposed Ahlus-Sunnah and agreed with the Khawarij on that, and both groups have strayed from the right path.
The correct view is the first one, which is the position of Ahlus-Sunnah wal-Jama'ah: that he is a sinner with weak faith and is in great danger of Allah's wrath and punishment, but he is not a disbeliever with major kufr, which is apostasy from Islam. Nor will he abide in the Fire forever like the disbelievers if he dies upon any of these sins. Rather, he is subject to Allah's will: if He wills, He will forgive him; if He wills, He will punish him according to the sins upon which he died, then He will bring him out of the Fire. None will abide therein forever except the disbelievers. Then, after the punishment Allah has decreed for him has passed, Allah will bring him out of the Fire into Paradise. This is the statement of the people of truth, and this is what has been reported in mutawatir narrations from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, contrary to the Khawarij and Mu'tazilah. Allah says: ⟦Q1⟧ [An-Nisa:48]. He, Glorified be He, has made what is less than shirk subject to His will, Mighty and Majestic.
As for one who dies upon major shirk, he will abide in the Fire forever, and Paradise is forbidden for him, because Allah, Glorified be He, says: ⟦Q2⟧ [Al-Ma'idah:72]. And He, Glorified be He, says: ⟦Q3⟧ [At-Tawbah:17]. The verses on this meaning are many.
As for the sinner, if he enters the Fire, he remains in it as long as Allah wills, and he does not abide like the disbelievers. However, his stay may be prolonged, and this is a specific, temporary abiding, not like the abiding of the disbelievers, as He, Glorified be He, said in the verse of Al-Furqan when He mentioned the polytheist, the murderer, and the adulterer: ⟦Q4⟧ [Al-Furqan:68-69]. It is a temporary abiding that has an end.
As for the polytheist, his abiding is perpetual, forever, and for this reason He, Mighty and Majestic, said concerning the polytheists in Surat Al-Baqarah: ⟦Q5⟧ [Al-Baqarah:167]. And He, Glorified be He, said in Surat Al-Ma'idah concerning the disbelievers: ⟦Q6⟧ [Al-Ma'idah:37]⟦N7⟧.
(Majmu' Fatawa wa Maqalat al-Shaykh Ibn Baz 5/338)
